brief: Why ambition is overrated — 6 reframes from people who burned out and started over.

slots.scriptTagline: from people who burned out and rebuilt slow

slots.body: You don't earn rest by collapsing. The top performers you admire schedule recovery like it is non-negotiable. Stop when your body whispers, not when it screams.
Massive ambition often masks a fear of the present. Pick one small promise and keep it. Momentum lives in completed tasks, not in grand visions that paralyze you.
Burnout survivors say the crash hurt most because they had nowhere else to belong. Start a life where work is one chapter, not the entire book. You are allowed to be mediocre at something you love.
Ambition makes you say yes to everyone else's timeline. Recovery starts when you treat your own calendar as sacred. The most successful rebuilds began with brutal subtraction.
Constant striving is a treadmill disguised as a ladder. Boredom creates the space where your real values can finally surface. Let your next chapter be deliberately unimpressive for a while.
Ambition sold you the idea that you are a project to be completed. You were never broken; you were just exhausted from chasing moving finish lines. Stop. You have done enough today.
